question: Does the newer detailed prompt-action pattern materially reduce execution durability compared with the older compact direct Build Colony + Durable Execution command, and is task volume/agent overload the cause?
epistemic_rules: Valid HUMAN_GATE/provider failure is not execution-continuity failure.
Prompt length is not treated as a causal variable without counterfactual evidence.

compact_direct_system_invocation.command_shape: direct Build Colony run + Durable Execution across all admissible frontiers
direct Build Colony run + Durable Execution across all admissible software frontiers
evidence: FAE-testnet commit bb875a8092c987f0b6097be708e570e86e5411 (verified Build Colony closure)
FAE-testnet commit b29b5e43937c4a5a4ff6e61b319520d1d629ae1a (close admissible Durable frontiers)

detailed_prompt_action.command_shape: large evidence-first prompt with challenge method, CII/Build Colony/Durable sequencing and extensive constraints
evidence: FAE-testnet commit c79e131d87b4af35a1ce4415c7bfb59dcbb66cde (Build Colony run manifest)
FAE-testnet commit c2b0f2cff2caefedb280321d9b0b141e2ef15108 (Durable review checkpoint closure)

detailed_prompt_action.workstream: FAE — DP6 Robust Premise Review / RP-B3-T1
detailed_prompt_action.command_shape: large bounded technical continuation prompt with exact branch/SHA/evidence constraints
evidence: provider run 36654718186 fail-closed at frontend compatibility boundary

detailed_prompt_action.command_shape: detailed Project Assurance bounded-local-validation action prompt
evidence: Latest observed Red-Team workflow remains unrelated run 35408954783

detailed_prompt_action.workstream: FAE — Browser-Coin Design Assurance Review (initial launch attempt)
detailed_prompt_action.command_shape: detailed cross-system prompt requesting CII/Build Colony/Durable
evidence: Initial Continuity Check found no branch, Build Colony artifact or Durable checkpoint before later successful relaunch

perception.explanation: There was a real increase in observable interruption/no-first-artifact cases around some prompt-action launches, but the effect is not universal and is not explained by prompt length alone.

evidence: Browser-Coin Design Assurance used a highly detailed prompt yet produced admission, Build Colony manifest, Durable state, seven-challenge report and canonical merge.
RP-B3-T1 used a highly detailed prompt yet produced real execution, provider failure evidence and resumable checkpoints.
Compact direct runs also experienced occasional crashes/provider failures while still preserving continuity.

first_proven_difference.name: distance_to_first_persistent_artifact
first_proven_difference.explanation: Compact commands make Build Colony execution the first operational imperative. Prompt-action messages often place reconstruction, classification, conditional system selection and authority interpretation before launch materialization.

mechanism: More pre-launch decision nodes before any durable write
Conditional language such as when-applicable/if-needed can leave no single mandatory executor
Multiple subsystem handoffs can leave ownership of the first artifact implicit
Narrative context can be correctly understood without that understanding being equivalent to executor invocation

evidence: Earlier BrowserCoin DI localized first divergence at explicit_execution_order -> execution_admission/materialized_launch.
General Execution subsequently added ELG-01 execution launch admission.
ELG-01 defines immutable ADMITTED/HUMAN_GATE/REJECTED/FAILED_BEFORE_LAUNCH receipts and requires owner/repository/executor bindings.
The durable ELG-01 host persists receipts but explicitly does not create authority or trigger an executor.
launch_handshake_gap.implication: The historical silent-loss mode was real. ELG-01 improves observability/fail-closed semantics, but by design it does not itself guarantee that Build Colony or another executor actually starts.

user_prompt_style_effect.explanation: Assistant-generated prompt-action text can worsen the risk when it over-specifies the task graph but fails to make launch materialization the first mandatory operation. The harmful property is orchestration indirection without an immediate persistent handshake, not verbosity itself.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The agent is simply overloaded by the number of tasks in long prompts.
Detailed prompts are generally less effective than compact prompts.
Durable Execution itself is the original cause of the interruptions.
All interruptions reflect a continuity defect.
ruled_out.explanation: Some stops are correct fail-closed provider/technical/human/external gates.

smallest_operational_change_without_syst.description: For future action prompts, keep the rich context but make the first imperative a mandatory idempotent execution-launch materialization before reconstruction or substantive work.
template_semantics: Materialize this run identity/launch receipt first.
Bind owner, repository, executor and authority envelope.
If launch cannot be admitted, persist HUMAN_GATE/REJECTED/FAILED_BEFORE_LAUNCH instead of continuing narratively.
After ADMITTED, invoke Build Colony immediately when requested.
Then use Durable Execution across every admissible frontier without asking to proceed.
Stop only at genuine human authority, external/provider wait, fail-closed technical boundary or terminal closure.
smallest_operational_change_without_syst.note: This does not require making prompts shorter. It changes ordering and makes persistence precede analysis.

cii_needed.reason: ELG-01 has already been designed and canonicalized in General Execution. A future CII should be justified only if evidence shows admitted launch receipts still fail to produce executor-side first artifacts.
